title: Metamorphic Testing for Fairness Evaluation in Large Language Models: Identifying Intersectional Bias in LLaMA and GPT

bias_targets.methodology: Applying Metamorphic Testing (MT) by adding, removing, or substituting combinations of multiple sensitive attributes (e.g., race, age, gender, religion) in prompts, and measuring unintended variations in the model's response using fine-tuned BERT models for sentiment and tone analysis.
Generating test cases using templates with placeholders for religious identities (e.g., Christianity, Islam, Buddhism) and evaluating output tone and sentiment invariance.
Using Metamorphic Relations (MRs) to swap ethnic identities (e.g., Caucasian, African-American, Asian, Hispanic) in conversational prompts to identify fluctuations in output sentiment and tone.

Modifying social status (e.g., upper-class, lower-class) and economic conditions (e.g., low-income, unemployed) in test prompts and evaluating changes in model responses using sentiment and tone classification.
Substituting political views (e.g., conservative, liberal, socialist) in source test cases and tracking whether the model maintains consistent sentiment and tone.
Replacing professions (e.g., teacher, engineer, lawyer) in conversational templates and applying tone and sentiment analysis to detect output inconsistencies.
Testing model fairness by varying the spoken language attribute (e.g., English, Spanish, Arabic) of the subject in the prompt and analyzing the resulting sentiment and tone.
Altering the marital status (e.g., single, married, divorced) in test cases and comparing the generated responses' tone and sentiment against the source responses.
Applying substitution and removal Metamorphic Relations (MRs) on gender attributes (e.g., male, female) in test cases and analyzing the model outputs for sentiment or tonal shifts.
Varying age-related descriptors (e.g., young, elderly, 30-year-old) via Metamorphic Testing to identify disparities in language model sentiment and tone.
